links.outcome: Multidisciplinary FMEA/FTA identification of application-specific failure modes in AI-driven radiotherapy workflow
links.effect: Eight-expert team identified 86 failure modes across 5 steps and 28 sub-steps; 25 high-risk FMs identified, mostly in ROI delineation, with human error the primary factor.
links.quote: After removing duplicates, a total of 25 high‐risk FMs were identified, which should be given special attention when developing QM standards.

links.outcome: Failure modes from unverified AI auto-contouring outputs (spurious points, wrong slices, omitted ROIs)
links.effect: Ignored spurious points had the highest QM-free RPN (186.2); 14 of 25 high-risk FMs involved ROI delineation, which relies on AI. Human error was the primary factor.
links.quote: Therefore, doctors should avoid blindly or completely relying on AI models.

links.outcome: Risk reduction (RPN) from QM measures such as automated verification, checklists, and regular QA
links.effect: RPN fell from 55.80 ± 38.40 (QM-free) to 16.17 ± 10.99 (QM), p < 0.001; spurious points RPN fell from 186.2 to 35.3. TPS-TDS communication errors saw smaller reductions.
links.quote: The difference in RPN between the two evaluation groups was statistically significant ( p < 0.001), confirming the effectiveness of QM measures and demonstrating that the proposed QM measures can effectively reduce the risk of AIO for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

links.outcome: Effect of dual verification by doctor and physicist on high-risk auto-contouring failure modes
links.effect: Dual verification and automated verification were the QM measures applied to high-risk ROI errors; overall RPN dropped significantly with QM measures (55.80 to 16.17, p < 0.001), though not tested individually.
links.quote: We employed an automated pre‐planning quality check of all ROIs as a QM measure to address this FM, overcoming the drawbacks of time‐consuming and ineffective visual inspection.

automated software verification of AI-generated contours

models_evaluated: uRT-TPOIS automated contouring and treatment planning modules

links.effect: FMEA identified 86 failure modes in the AIO workflow.
links.quote: After FMEA analysis, 86 FMs were identified.

links.effect: Mean RPN was 55.80 ± 38.40 without QM and 16.17 ± 10.99 with QM.
links.quote: The results showed that the RPN for the QM‐free group was 55.80 ± 38.40, and for the QM group was 16.17 ± 10.99.

links.effect: Automated pre-planning ROI check reduced RPN from 186.2 to 35.3.
links.quote: This significantly reduced its RPN from 186.2 to 35.3, substantially decreasing the risk associated with this FM.

links.effect: 14 of 25 high-risk FMs were associated with “Delineating the ROIs.”
links.quote: Among the 25 high‐risk FMs, 14 are associated with the main step of “Delineating the ROIs.”

links.effect: Among high-risk FMs, human error was primary; inadequate training followed.
links.quote: Among all high‐risk FMs, human error was the primary factor, followed by inadequate training, software/hardware errors, and communication deficiencies, indicating that the main factors affecting the safety and effectiveness of AIO were operational norms in various steps and the team's familiarity with the workflow.

links.effect: TPS communication errors with TDS had less significant RPN decreases after QM.
links.quote: However, there were still some FMs (highlighted in red boxes) with less significant decreases in RPN after implementing QM measures, including TPS communication errors with TDS, discovery of significant setup errors in image guidance, and failure to create in vivo plans.
